title: Component lifecycle record
description: The component lifecycle record, as defined in The Software Field Guide, issue #105: the lifecycle chapter's YAML — the paper trail of a component's versioned transitions, each carrying the evidence its type demands. A bake carries the sha256 image digest it produced; a patch carries the provenance (source and commit) of the change folded in; an upgrade carries the rehearsed rollback's rehearsal date. The record is owned, versioned, and reviewed, and the review must be fresh (365 days) and cover every transition on it: a transition recorded once and never refreshed is a question, not a fact. Judged at the lifecycle gate against the component package manifest (joined by component name), as a conformance gate — not an advisor: a record documenting a component the manifest never packaged is refused. This schema mirrors the shape rules of the Rego validator (policies/lifecycle); the validator additionally enforces the semantic rules a JSON schema cannot — reviewedOn and every recordedOn/rehearsedOn a real calendar date not in the future, the review no older than 365 days, every transition recorded on or before the review, no two transitions of one type sharing a recorded date, and the component mismatch judged at the join.

version.description: The record's version. The lifecycle record is versioned like the component it tracks.

reviewedOn.description: Date the record was last reviewed, YYYY-MM-DD. The validator flags reviews older than 365 days, dates in the future, and transitions recorded after the review.

owner.description: The team that owns the record. A paper trail without an owner is a trail nobody maintains.

component.description: The name of the component the record tracks. The gate joins the record to the component package manifest by this name.

transitions.description: The component's versioned transitions in the order they were recorded. Each row names its type — bake, patch, or upgrade — the date it was recorded, and carries the evidence its type demands.

type.description: The transition's type. The gate vouches for bake (an image built), patch (a change folded in), and upgrade (a replacement installed); anything else is a fact this gate cannot judge.

recordedOn.description: The date the transition was recorded, YYYY-MM-DD. A transition the record's review never saw is a fact nobody re-checked; the validator requires recordedOn on or before the record's reviewedOn.

imageDigest.description: Bake evidence: the sha256 digest of the image the bake produced. A bake with no digest is an image nobody can pin to what actually runs.

provenance.description: Patch evidence: where the change came from, and which commit built it. A patch without provenance is a change nobody authored.

source.description: The source control repository the change came from.

commit.description: The commit the change was built from. A patch pinned to no commit is a change that can point anywhere.

rollback.description: Upgrade evidence: the rehearsed way back. An upgrade nobody rehearsed the rollback for is a bet, not a transition.

rehearsedOn.description: The date the rollback was rehearsed, YYYY-MM-DD. A way back rehearsed tomorrow is a way back nobody has walked; the validator requires a real date not in the future.
